candidates.decision_relevance: The analyses repeatedly compare rolling breadth snapshots whose constituent membership changes, and sometimes conflict with separate breadth proxies. A consistently defined, timestamped constituent-level history would make breadth changes and their timing relative to price moves observable without treating mismatched snapshots as a trend.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs for 2026-10-30 and 2026-10-31 describe changing membership hashes, non-synchronous breadth snapshots, and unconfirmed canonical breadth; W37 weekly reviews also identify missing breadth construction and time alignment.
candidates.missing_history_problem: No comparable constituent-level breadth series across prior days or weeks is supplied; changing-membership snapshots cannot establish whether participation deterioration preceded, followed, or persisted through price weakness.

candidates.decision_relevance: Daily analyses often have only one settled session, which cannot show whether flows persisted or how they aligned with price and participation. A dated history of settled BTC and ETH flows would make multi-session flow direction and sequencing auditable.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs from 2026-10-30 through 2026-11-01 repeatedly characterize ETF evidence as a single settled session; weekly reviews report settled weekly totals but note missing granular sequences and timing.
candidates.metric_name: Settled BTC and ETH ETF flow history
candidates.missing_history_problem: The supplied daily captures do not provide a continuous, consistently dated sequence of settled flows, limiting assessment of persistence and alignment with observed market paths.

candidates.decision_relevance: Historical reviews cannot reliably distinguish ex-ante evidence from hindsight when forecast definitions, issuance times, freeze-time inputs, and linked matured outcomes are omitted or unavailable. Preserving these records would enable candidate-specific audit of timing, range outcomes, and warning cohorts without changing decision semantics.
candidates.evidence_reference: Weekly reviews W34-W43 report missing candidate objects, timestamps, bounds, or linked outcome rows; daily outputs provide candidates but describe them as unratified and historical calibration as descriptive.
candidates.metric_name: Frozen candidate and outcome provenance records
candidates.missing_history_problem: Past candidate specifications and their exact information cutoffs are not consistently available alongside the corresponding matured outcomes, preventing reliable ex-ante scoring and hindsight-leakage checks.
